**TL;DR**

- **The Fed held and the tape barely flinched.** The FOMC kept the target range at **3.75%–4.00%** on a **10–2 vote — both dissents wanted a hike** —
- and all three majors closed up a third straight day: **S&P 500 7,743.98 +0.28%**, **Nasdaq Composite 26,549.85 +0.27%**, **Dow 52,475.10 +0.19%**, **Russell 2000 2,830.51 +0.41%**.
- **The curve bear-steepened on the hold.** 10-year **5.05% (+6bp)**, 2-year **4.67% (−3bp)**, 30-year **5.37% (+7bp)** — the 2s10s widened to **+38bp from +29bp**.
- The 2-year *falling* while the long end *rose* is the market pricing out hikes, not growth.
- **Oil was the day's other live wire.** WTI futures **+2.6% to $102.55** at 4 p.m. on Yemen fighting and renewed-strike fear around Iran; **USO +1.64%**.
- **Breadth was much weaker than the headline.** **RSP −0.04% vs SPY +0.34%** — a 38bp gap —
- and the equal-weight S&P was *down* on a day the cap-weighted index was up. Volume **17.06B shares** (CBOE consolidated, 17:35 ET) versus a 17.18B 20-day average, so no volume thrust.
- **Tech led on a memory/AI-infrastructure bid.** **XLK +0.79%** was the best sector;
- SK Hynix's record quarter sent Seoul to its best day in three months and **MU +5.86%, SNDK +7.66%, LRCX +5.39%** led the chip complex.
- **VRT +16.48%** on a beat-and-raise and **ORCL +10.73%** on its investor day. Laggards were the rate-sensitive complex: **XLU −0.85%, XLRE −0.73%, XLC −0.42%**.
- **After-hours is where the story actually is, and it is a violent software/AI-capex repricing.** **Alphabet −9.97%** (first top-and-bottom-line miss in nearly four years, free cash flow **−$9.07B**) versus **Microsoft +2.88%** (Azure +48%).
- Then the contagion: **NOW −18.10%, FTNT −25.71%, SFM −22.98%**, and a broad SaaS/cyber unwind (**CRWD −6.44%, PANW −6.41%, ZS −6.08%, CRM −5.58%**).
- Off the beaten path, **LITE +8.65%** on the report that **Marvell is in talks to buy it** (MRVL −8.40%).

**5. After-hours earnings reactions**

**Alphabet (GOOGL) — **-9.97% to $292.50** — a rare miss, and the FCF line is the story**

- Q3 revenue **$127.58B vs $128.22B** expected; adjusted EPS also missed. **First top-and-bottom-line miss in nearly four years** (CappNotes).
- **Search revenue $63.35B vs $64.96B expected**; search growth decelerated to **12% from 17%** the prior quarter.
- **Google Cloud +103%** to $30.71B — the growth engine was fine.
- **Free cash flow −$9.07B.** FY capex guidance held at **$195–205B**.
- Reaction: **-9.97%** at the last print; if it holds, it is the stock's **largest single-day drop in three years**.
- Options had priced a **5.8%** implied move — the realized move is roughly **4 points beyond the implied** (Cboe LiveVol via EconoTimes).
- GOOG (Class C) **-9.75%**; GOOGN **-6.18%**.

**Microsoft (MSFT) — **+2.88% to $546.30** — the counterweight**

- Fiscal Q1 revenue **$92.28B (+19%) vs $90.69B** expected; adjusted EPS **$4.89 vs $4.73**.
- **Azure +48%** to $33.2B, above its own forecast, with ~49% guided for Q2.
- **Capex $45.2B vs ~$50.7B expected** — the miss everyone talks about, attributed to third-party capacity delivery delays; full-year targets reiterated. Operating cash flow ~$58B.
- Note the intraday path: the gain widened past +5% and narrowed to +2.5% before settling near +2.9% (r/wallstreetbets live thread).

**Fortinet (FTNT) — **-25.71% to $129.33** — beat-and-raise, sold anyway**

- Top and bottom line beat; **revenue +20% to $2.08B**; FY26 revenue forecast raised to ~20% growth — but **the smallest of its three 2026 raises** —
- and **the service-revenue forecast was cut**.
- Non-GAAP gross margin **79.6% vs 80.1%** expected.
- The stock had already lost **-5.90%** in the regular session, so the total two-day move is roughly **-30%**;
- the AH print of $129.33 is also below the bottom of its 52-week range.

**ServiceNow (NOW) — **-18.10% to $122.95** — two cents of EPS**

- Q3 adjusted EPS **$1.00 vs $1.02** consensus; Q4 subscription revenue guidance **$4.245–4.255B** vs $4.25B consensus — in line.
- The damage came from **cRPO** and the "AI disrupts software" narrative, not the guide.
- Two-day move from the prior close is **-20.59%**, and the decline exceeded the options-implied move by roughly **8-9 points**.

**Sprouts Farmers Market (SFM) — **-22.98% to $47.75** — the guidance did the damage**

- EPS **$1.21 vs $1.23**; revenue **$2.30B vs $2.33B**; **comps -0.9%** with **transactions -3.3%**; gross margin -50bp.
- **Q4 EPS guide $0.47–0.51** against a ~$1.21 consensus; **FY26 EPS cut to ~$4.80 vs ~$5.53** estimated.
- Management: "Traffic, units, and frequency are not recovering, even against easier compares." Shares broke below the 52-week low of $60.47.
- XLP was **+1.32% in after-hours**, so the move is company-specific, not staples-wide.

**Lumentum (LITE) / Marvell (MRVL) — **+8.65% / -8.40%** — M&A, not earnings**

- Bloomberg: **Marvell is in late-stage talks to buy Lumentum**, an announcement possible as early as next week; no final agreement. LITE market cap ~$83B vs MRVL ~$221B.
- Neither had a release or filing. LITE was already +5.52% in the regular session.

**Chipotle (CMG) — **+7.00% to $30.74** — comps beat**

- **Same-store sales +2.1% vs +1.5% expected.**

**The three things that set the tone tomorrow:**

- **Does the software contagion spread to cash open?** The AH tape had 30+ software/SaaS/cyber names down 5-7% while QQQ's own AH print was only -1.05% (718.00).
- If the cash open follows the *names* rather than the *index*, this is a de-rating day; if it follows QQQ and the Nasdaq-100 futures (-1.56%), it is a one-name shock.
- **GDP and PCE against a Fed that just held with two hike-dissents.** A 3.0% GDP print with core PCE at 3.1% keeps the 2-year yield (4.67%) from easing further;
- a soft print revives the easing trade that drove today's 2-year rally.
- **Amazon's capex and FCF.** Alphabet's miss was as much about negative free cash flow and $195–205B of capex as about EPS.
- Amazon is the next company asked to defend that spend.
